label: prf:interface-knot-markov-z
title: Proof of interface knot markov z
html:
(Markov axiom and Hecke skein.)

For a positive interface generator \sigma_g, the Markov axiom (Existence and non-degeneracy of the Markov trace (Jones, 1987)) gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \cdot \sigma_g) \;=\; z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha)
  \qquad \forall\, \alpha \in H_{n}(q).

For a negative interface generator \sigma_g^{-1}, the Hecke skein relation \sigma_g^{-1} = \sigma_g - h \cdot \mathbf{1} combined with linearity of \mathrm{tr}_M gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \cdot \sigma_g^{-1})
  \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \cdot \sigma_g) - h \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha)
  \;=\; (z - h) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha).

These two identities apply when the interface generator is the last letter. In \mathcal{B}_K an interface generator sits between two blocks, so the iteration needs a block-multiplicativity lemma.

Lemma (block multiplicativity). Let x \in H_{k+1}(q), let y \in H_m(q), and let \mathrm{sh}_{k+1}(y) be y with every \sigma_i replaced by \sigma_{i+k+1}. Then

  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,\mathrm{sh}_{k+1}(y)\bigr) = \mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y),
  \qquad
  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,\sigma_k\,\mathrm{sh}_{k+1}(y)\bigr) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y).

Proof. Put a = x or a = x\sigma_k; in both cases a lies in H_{k+2}(q). Consider the linear map y \mapsto \mathrm{tr}_M(a\,\mathrm{sh}_{k+1}(y)). For m = 1 it gives \mathrm{tr}_M(a). For m \ge 2, write a basis element of H_m(q) as T_u\,\sigma_{m-1}\,T_v with u, v \in S_{m-1}, or as T_u with u \in S_{m-1}. In the first case \mathrm{sh}(T_v)\,a\,\mathrm{sh}(T_u) lies in H_{m+k}(q), so cyclicity, the Markov property for the top generator \sigma_{m+k}, and cyclicity again give

  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(a\,\mathrm{sh}(T_u)\,\sigma_{m+k}\,\mathrm{sh}(T_v)\bigr)
  = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(\mathrm{sh}(T_v)\,a\,\mathrm{sh}(T_u)\bigr)
  = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(a\,\mathrm{sh}(T_u T_v)\bigr).

In the second case \mathrm{sh}(T_u) lies in H_{m+k}(q) and the trace restricts. This is the same recursion that computes \mathrm{tr}_M(y) from \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1, so the map equals \mathrm{tr}_M(a)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y). The Markov property gives \mathrm{tr}_M(x\sigma_k) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x). \square

Now write \mathcal{B}_K = b_1\,\varepsilon_1\,b_2\,\varepsilon_2 \cdots \varepsilon_{A-1}\,b_A, where b_i is the word of the i-th nucleon on its own block of strands and \varepsilon_i = \sigma_{g_i}^{\pm 1} joins blocks i and i+1; the vacuum braid is b_1 b_2 \cdots b_A. Applying the lemma A - 1 times, with \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - h for the negative connectors, gives \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K) = z^{p_+}(z-h)^{p_-} \prod_i \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i), and \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K^{\mathrm{vac}}) = \prod_i \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i). Dividing yields the boxed identity (\star). An exact check over \mathbb{Q} at q = 2 (three blocks on nine strands, one positive and one negative connector) reproduces z(z-h).

Averaged (bar-invariant) p-n interface

The same single Markov input fixes a third interface factor. The canonical p-n boundary (closed_form_tau_M.canonical_interface_kinds, the averaging-resonance rule) carries no preferred chirality, so it is the bar-invariant (q \leftrightarrow q^{-1} symmetric) crossing

  \sigma_{\mathrm{bar}} \;:=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(\sigma_g + \sigma_g^{-1}\bigr)
  \;=\; \sigma_g - \tfrac{h}{2}\cdot\mathbf{1},

the last equality again from the Hecke skein \sigma_g^{-1} = \sigma_g - h. Linearity of \mathrm{tr}_M then gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha\cdot\sigma_{\mathrm{bar}})
  \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha\cdot\sigma_g) - \tfrac{h}{2}\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha)
  \;=\; \Bigl(z - \tfrac{h}{2}\Bigr)\cdot\mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha).

Thus all three per-interface factors — z (positive), z-h (negative), z-\tfrac{h}{2} (bar-invariant p-n) — follow by trace-linearity from the single Markov axiom \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha\sigma_g) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) plus the skein \sigma_g^{-1}=\sigma_g-h; none is an independent input or a fit. The division-free form \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha(\sigma_g+\sigma_g^{-1})) = (2z-h)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) holds over any commutative ring (the \tfrac12 normalisation is deferred to the archimedean realisation, per the base-ring convention).

The three factors are one bar-orbit

Writing \overline{\phantom{x}} for the involution q \mapsto q^{-1}, the positive and negative factors are bar-conjugates of each other:

  \overline{z} \;=\; \frac{q^{-3}}{q^{-2}+1} \;=\; \frac{1}{q\,(q^{2}+1)}
  \;=\; z - h .

So f_{pp} = z and f_{nn} = \overline{z}, and the p-n factor is exactly their mean,

  z - \tfrac{h}{2} \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(z + \overline{z}\bigr),

which is the bar-symmetriser of z — manifestly bar-even. The name "bar-invariant p-n interface" is therefore literal rather than descriptive: the p-n factor is not merely a bar-invariant choice, it is the bar-symmetrisation of the p-p factor.

This also fixes where a flavour weighting can act. The colour-tube-weighted form of the p-n factor is the same mean, tilted:

  z - h\Bigl(\tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{\delta}{4}\Bigr)
  \;=\; w_{p}\, f_{pp} + w_{n}\, f_{nn},
  \qquad
  w_{p} = \tfrac{1}{2} + \tfrac{\delta}{4},
  \quad
  w_{n} = \tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{\delta}{4},
  \quad
  w_{p} + w_{n} = 1,

with \delta the substrate flavour split of the substrate flavor split conjecture. A like-flavour bond has no mean to tilt — averaging f_{pp} with itself returns f_{pp} for any weights summing to one — which is why the weighting is defined at the p-n interface and nowhere else.

The tilt is not bar-invariant. \delta is bar-mixed, \overline{\delta} = -q^{2}\delta, and

  \overline{f^{\,\mathrm{weighted}}_{pn}} - f^{\,\mathrm{weighted}}_{pn}
  \;=\; \frac{(q-1)^{5}(q+1)^{3}(q^{2}+1)}{12\,q^{5}},

nonzero for q \neq 1 (about 1.67 \times 10^{-5} at the substrate anchor). The unweighted factor above is the only one of the two that is bar-even, and the derivation in this proof — trace-linearity from the single Markov axiom — yields that one. The weighted form requires \delta as an additional input and is therefore not obtained here.

The obstruction is one factor of q^{2}, and it is repairable

Write a general weighted p-n factor with offset \varepsilon, f_{pn}(\varepsilon) = (\tfrac12 + \varepsilon) f_{pp} + (\tfrac12 - \varepsilon) f_{nn}. Since f_{nn} = \overline{f_{pp}}, the involution swaps the two terms, so

  \overline{f_{pn}} - f_{pn}
  \;=\; -\bigl(\overline{\varepsilon} + \varepsilon\bigr)\,\frac{q^{2}-1}{q},

which vanishes iff \overline{\varepsilon} = -\varepsilon — the offset must be bar-odd. (Not bar-even: symmetrising the weight is the wrong repair.)

The colour weighting uses \varepsilon = \delta/4, and \overline{\delta} = -q^{2}\delta, so it misses bar-oddness by exactly a factor of q^{2} and nothing else. That factor localises: in the factored form \delta \sim \hbar_q^{2}\, h_q\, [2]_q of the closed and factored forms of the substrate flavor split, the Hecke crossing h_q is already bar-odd and the doublet integer [2]_q is bar-even, so the entire obstruction is the \hbar_q^{2} prefactor — the two quanta of substrate Planck action.

Consequently a bar-invariant colour weighting exists: \varepsilon = q\,\delta\,E/4 is bar-odd for any bar-even E, since \overline{q\delta} = -q\delta. Two natural members are E = 1 and E = [2]_q/2 (the latter being the bar-odd projection of \delta), differing from the current offset by 11–12 % and hence by order 8 \times 10^{-6} in f_{pn}.

Bar-invariance is necessary but not sufficient. It fixes the parity and leaves a whole bar-even function E free, so it does not by itself determine the weighting; selecting E requires re-deriving the colour weighting from the colour-tube geometry, and no particular E is asserted here. All of the above is checked in exact arithmetic (17 assertions), and the four identities that are field-theoretic rather than substrate-specific — \overline{z} = z - h, the bar-symmetriser form, the bar defect -(\overline{\varepsilon} + \varepsilon)h, and the bar-even-iff-offset-bar-odd equivalence — are proved over an arbitrary characteristic-zero field.

Full-trace verification at z = q^3/(q^2+1) (4 atoms)

The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M is evaluated as \sum_\lambda y_\lambda\,\chi_\lambda with the two-row weights at z = q^3/(q^2+1) and Hoefsmit characters in MPFR at q_0, for H_n with n \in \{6, 9, 12\}; averaged letters are expanded by linearity, and the route is checked against the independent Markov-ascent trace before use. Census word (p-n interface =\sigma_g, as listed below):

atom A p_+ p_- \mathrm{tr}_M^{\mathrm{FULL}}/\mathrm{tr}_M^{\mathrm{CONSTIT}} predicted z^{p_+}(z-h)^{p_-} rel. err.
D 2 1 0 0.61268804 0.61268804 4\times10^{-51}
T 3 1 1 0.24729789 0.24729789 2\times10^{-50}
{}^{3}He 3 2 0 0.37538663 0.37538663 3\times10^{-50}
{}^{4}He 4 2 1 0.15151646 0.15151646 4\times10^{-51}

The live canonical word carries the bar-invariant colour-weighted p-n letter \sigma_g - h(\tfrac12 - \tfrac{\delta}{4}) instead of \sigma_g; with that factor in place of z the ratios are \approx 0.50822979, 0.20513564, 0.31138631 and 0.12568415, again equal to the predicted product to \le 5\times10^{-50} (and likewise for the colour-blind \sigma_g - h/2). The identity (\star) therefore holds at z = q^3/(q^2+1) on every word tested, at the 10^{-50} floor of the arithmetic.

Per-atom interface census (from the canonical atom braid word):

  • D: p \cdot \sigma_3 \cdot n — 1 positive (p-n).
  • T: p \cdot \sigma_3 \cdot n \cdot \sigma_6^{-1} \cdot n — 1 positive (p-n) + 1 negative (n-n).
  • {}^{3}He: p \cdot \sigma_3 \cdot p \cdot \sigma_6 \cdot n — 2 positive (p-p, p-n).
  • {}^{4}He: p \cdot \sigma_3 \cdot p \cdot \sigma_6 \cdot n \cdot \sigma_9^{-1} \cdot n — 2 positive (p-p, p-n) + 1 negative (n-n).

Structural reading

The interface knot \bowtie_K is categorically the Markov-axiom boundary contribution to the canonical atomic braid:

  • Positive interface \sigma_g (p-p or p-n boundary) \to factor z exactly (single application of the Markov axiom).
  • Negative interface \sigma_g^{-1} (n-n boundary, antisymmetric quark pair) \to factor z - h exactly (Markov axiom + Hecke skein \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - h \cdot \mathbf{1}).

The crossing-sign / nucleon-flavor pairing is encoded in \bowtie_K via p_+(K) and p_-(K) counts — these are determined structurally by the canonical-braid construction, not phenomenologically fit.

This locks 's interface-knot factorisation as derivation-grade: each interface in the canonical atomic braid contributes a Markov-trace factor that is either z or z - h, determined by the crossing sign. No empirical-fit parameter remains at the \mathrm{tr}_M level.

Constit-side companion identity (conjectural)

The factorisation (\star) isolates the interface contribution to the \mathrm{tr}_M ratio. The complementary constit factor — \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K^{\mathrm{vac}}) at varying Z — admits its own clean categorical form at the substrate point:

  \frac{\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\beta_{(Z+1, N)}^{\mathrm{constit}}\bigr)}
       {\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\beta_{(Z, N)}^{\mathrm{constit}}\bigr)}
  \;=\; (2q - 1) \,+\, O(h^4)
  \quad\text{at }q_0.

This is the content of the conjectured constituent factor 2q - 1, whose 0.033\% agreement was measured at the half-argument weight \sqrt{q}/(q+1) on the grouped intra-nucleon word.

The step does not survive at z = q^3/(q^2+1). The constituent product is multiplicative over disjoint strand blocks (checked to 10^{-50}), so the constituent step is the single-proton trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_p). At z = q^3/(q^2+1) and q_0 this is \approx 0.62932840 on the canonical (alternating) word and \approx 1.14575969 on the grouped word, against 2q_0 - 1 \approx 1.21995717: misses of 48.4\% and 6.1\%. The full per-Z step on the canonical word is correspondingly \approx 0.38558198, not q^3(2q-1)/(q^2+1) \approx 0.7475. This is a scope-limited negative: the identification (2q-1) for the constituent factor does not hold at z = q^3/(q^2+1) for either intra-nucleon ordering; it says nothing about whether some other closed form describes the per-Z step.
